abortion.text: In an interview about abortion restrictions, she said medical decisions should be left to families, doctors, and faith.
abortion.quote: medical decisions should remain between families, doctors, and their faith.

tax.text: He supports closing tax loopholes and enforcing tax laws to collect revenue that is currently unpaid.
tax.quote: End tax loopholes and enforce our tax laws. Target the tax gap which is the amount of tax revenue not collected due to under reporting by individuals.

trade.text: Houser says tariffs can be useful in limited circumstances but argues current tariffs raise household costs and should be made more responsible.
trade.quote: I believe responsible tariffs are a useful tool in limited circumstances. However, we need to get back to responsible tariffs and reform our relationships with other countries who not only rely on us, but with whom we rely on for goods.

debt.text: Houser supports removing the Social Security payroll-tax cap to extend the fund’s viability and reduce the deficit.
debt.quote: Removing that cap so that we can extend the viability of the Social Security fund and quickly begin closing the funding gap to significantly reduce our overall deficit.

debt.text: His campaign platform includes funding Social Security.
debt.quote: -Ban foreign governments from buying American farmland -Fund Social Security -Ban Corporate Purchase of Single Family Homes

housing.text: As a Ketchum councilman, he moved approval of a preliminary plat for a workforce-housing project.
housing.quote: Motion to approve the Lot Consolidation Preliminary Plat for the ARCH Workforce Housing Project and adopt the Findings of Fact and Decision

tax.text: He said he would oppose increased taxes on the working class.
tax.quote: “No” to increased spending on warfare we cannot afford; “no” to subsidies for corporations, foreign governments, and the permanent able-bodied welfare class; and “no” to increased taxes on the working class.

debt.text: He says he would oppose any budget that increases the national debt and supports paying it down.
debt.quote: The only way to stop the bleed and halt the destruction of everyday Americans’ purchasing power is to balance the national budget and pay down the debt. In Congress, I will vote “No” on any budget that will increase the national debt.

immigration.text: He supports strong border enforcement and limiting H-2A visas, saying additional labor holds down wages.
immigration.quote: Johanson said the excess labor coming into the jobs keeps the wages low, and said he’d support limiting the number of visas in the program that are administered.

guns.text: His campaign stated that the Second Amendment should not be infringed.
guns.quote: Taxation? Theft. The Second Amendment? Shall not be infringed.

health.text: He attributes high health-care costs to limited competition and regulation, and supports deregulation and direct primary care.
health.quote: Johanson said a lack of competition and over-regulation have driven up healthcare costs.

energy.text: His candidate profile describes domestic drilling, fracking and mineral mining as ways to protect the environment.
energy.quote: Protect the environment by drilling, fracking, and mining essential minerals in the USA.

tax.text: Simpson says he strongly supports tax relief for families and job creators and has supported legislation to lower taxes.
tax.quote: I strongly support providing tax relief to American families and those who create jobs and grow our economy

wages.text: He voted against the Protecting the Right to Organize Act.
wages.quote: Vote Question: On Passage Protecting the Right to Organize Act

trade.text: He said he dislikes tariffs and hopes they are reduced worldwide.
trade.quote: hopefully in the long run, you’ll see tariffs worldwide reduced which I think will be a good thing for trade in this world.

debt.text: Simpson advocates major deficit reduction, spending cuts, tax reform, and changes to mandatory programs while preserving current beneficiaries’ benefits.
debt.quote: For years, I have advocated that Congress pursue a “go big” approach to deficit reduction that would find at least $4 trillion in savings by putting all options on the table.

housing.text: He supported legislation that expanded the low-income housing tax credit.
housing.quote: including supporting the “One Big Beautiful Bill,” which expands the low-income housing tax credit.

schools.text: Simpson supports education reforms giving parents more control and more informed choices about their children’s education.
schools.quote: I support steering education policy and reform toward more openness and transparency for parents to have more control and make more informed choices regarding their children’s education.

safety.text: He voted for legislation to equip law enforcement with less-lethal tools and technology.
safety.quote: There is no reason they shouldn’t be equipped with the most effective tools and technology available to protect themselves and our neighborhoods.

immigration.text: His campaign says he will support border security, a wall, and stopping illegal immigration.
immigration.quote: Securing the border and stopping illegal immigration is the most important issue facing our nation today.

guns.text: Simpson says he will oppose legislation requiring waiting periods or banning firearm ownership and supports Second Amendment rights.
guns.quote: I will not support any legislation that requires a waiting period for the purchase of a firearm, bans the ownership of firearms

abortion.text: Simpson describes himself as unapologetically pro-life and supports legislation restricting abortion and abortion funding.
abortion.quote: I am unapologetically pro-life, and I will continue to support legislation that recognizes the sanctity of human life and supports mothers.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: He voted for a bill requiring school athletics to recognize reproductive biology and genetics at birth.
gender.quote: There is no debate—biological men should never be competing in women's sports.

cannabis.text: He voted against House passage of the MORE Act.
cannabis.quote: Vote Question: On Passage MORE Act Vote Type: Yea-And-Nay

health.text: He voted for market-based health-care reforms intended to increase coverage choices and lower premiums.
health.quote: This legislation offers common-sense, market-based reforms to lower health care premium costs, expand access to quality care, provide every American with more options and flexibility to choose coverage that works for them, and bring greater transparency to America’s health care system.

energy.text: Simpson says energy policy should expand American-made energy and lower costs for families.
energy.quote: By securing our energy supply chain and ending reliance on foreign adversaries, we will not only strengthen our national security but also help lower costs for American families.

voting.text: He voted for a bill requiring photo ID for federal elections and proof of citizenship at registration.
voting.quote: Requiring photo identification and verifying United States citizenship when registering to vote in federal elections is not a controversial issue.

choices.name: C. Sierra - ID Law - Idaho Lorax

schools.text: He said school choice matters while also describing public education as essential, and answered neutral on a school-choice question.
schools.quote: The choice is important, but public education for the masses is to have a well-educated workforce. And without that, we will fail. Public schools like medical, they are evolving and are improving everywhere where it is allowed to flourish.

immigration.text: He supported securing the border while also identifying work permits, visitors, schooling, and marriage as immigration circumstances.
immigration.quote: Same as other countries, Work permits, visitors, schooling, and love and marriage--That's a difficult one to overcome!

guns.text: He emphasized the Second Amendment's right to bear arms and did not identify a specific restriction.
guns.quote: the simplified answer of the times was: To Bear Arms! But I prefer Bare Arm wrestling to resolve conflicts.

abortion.text: He described life as a priority but said the woman should have at least 51 percent of the choice in an elective-abortion decision.
abortion.quote: the male partner may have up to 49% of the vote or choice, while the woman-- who's life it is-- has at least 51% of the vote or choice.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: He agreed that biological males should not participate in women’s sports or occupy women’s spaces.
gender.quote: Biological males should not be allowed to participate in women's sports or occupy biological women's spaces whether it be bathrooms, locker rooms, sorority houses, women's shelters, or prison.

health.text: He endorsed universal health care, citing his experience living in countries with universal coverage.
health.quote: Sorry, but I have lived in Univeral healthcare countries. No one I've ever met would choose differently.

energy.text: He agreed that human-made climate change requires urgent political action and identified solar energy as the most reliable electricity source.
energy.quote: The sun. it still has a few billion years left, and fewer people.

voting.text: He agreed that some voters should be able to vote without photo ID, specifying small communities where people know one another.
voting.quote: Some. Small communities where most know each other. I use and affidavit.
